sense: in keeping with, as laid down by

evidence: Cic. Fin. 4.26: illī brevius secundum nātūram vīvere
Traupman 178: secundum lēgem, according to the law
terms.comment: With a person it means in someone’s favour: pontificēs secundum sē dēcrēvisse, that the pontiffs had decided for him (Cic. Att. 4.2.3, Lewis & Short). For “according to” a source, see the other sense.

evidence: Traupman 185, 270: ex foedere, according to the terms of the agreement
terms.comment: ex lēge, ex foedere; ex sententiā, as one wished, as planned.

phrases.latin: et conlaudāvī secundum facta et virtūtēs tuās
phrases.english: and I praised you as your deeds and merits deserve

phrases.latin: nāta est sententia veterum Acadēmicōrum et Peripatēticōrum, ut fīnem bonōrum dīcerent secundum nātūram vīvere
phrases.english: so arose the view of the Old Academy and the Peripatetics, who said that the highest good was to live according to nature

phrases.latin: rēbus tuīs tōtōque itinere ex sententiā cōnfectō nōs quam prīmum revīsās
phrases.english: when your business and the whole journey have gone according to plan, come back to us as soon as you can

sources: Lewis & Short: secundum · Lewis & Short: ex
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 178, 185, 270, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Livy 1, Cicero, De finibus 2 and 4 and Letters to Atticus 4–5, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026). Terence checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror), which follow the Oxford text: conlaudāvī is its spelling.
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
